CHAPTER IV

PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE

Article 5

1. Prevention of violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a is implemented through:a. planning and implementation of policies, programs, and activities; b. provision of education; andc. enhancement of community participation.
2. Prevention of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented by the Regional Government in an integrated and sustainable manner based on the Regional Long-Term Development Plan and the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
3. Planning and implementation of policies, programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a namely:a. integrating women and children protection issues into the policies, programs and activities of Regional Apparatus; andb. making women and children protection issues one of the regional development priorities.
4. Provision of education as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b namely: a. providing information, guidance and/or counseling; b. providing accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement and social services;
c. creating a friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women; andd. building and providing an easily accessible information system; (5) Enhancement of Community participation through involvement of parties as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, namely:a. building and enhancing community participation and awareness towards prevention of women and children protection; b. making regional regulations and encouraging Village Governments to make Village Regulations related to protection of women and children; andc. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, private sector/business world, universities, mass media, and non-governmental organizations as well as community institutions that work and care for women and children.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bulukumba Regency.
2. Government is a body or organization that exercises the governmental power of a state. The Government has the duty to administer governmental affairs, from the central, provincial, regency, municipal, sub-district, village, to hamlet levels.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an organization/Institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent in the context of administering government consisting of regional secretary, regional agencies and regional technical institutions, sub-districts, villages and civil service police units according to regional needs.
5. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the principal duties and functions in carrying out Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Bulukumba Regency.
6. Village Government is the administration of governmental affairs and the interests of the local community in the governmental system of the unitary state of the Republic of Indonesia.
7. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the annual financial plan of the regional government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and DPRD, and stipulated by Regional Regulation.
8. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBDes is the annual financial plan of the village government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Village Head and Village Representative Body which is stipulated through Village Regulation.

3 -

9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Implementation of Women's and Children's Protection is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Central Government, Regional Government, Village Government, and the community to fulfill the rights of women and children as citizens within the scope of this Regional Regulation.
11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women's and Children's Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
16. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, and deprivation of liberty arbitrarily whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
17. Victim is a person who experiences physical suffering, women and children who experience violence and/or mental threats and or economic loss resulting from an act of violence.
18. Victim of Violence is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from a criminal act of violence.
19. Violence Prevention is any action or effort undertaken to eliminate various factors that cause acts of violence against women and children.
20. Community is individual Indonesian citizens, community groups, and/or Mass Organizations.
21. Technical Implementation Unit for Women's and Children's Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an integrated service provider for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
22. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

4 -

23. Assistance for Victims of Violence is an effort or process to assist victims of violence in accessing the right to handling, protection, and recovery.
24. Rapid Reaction Team hereinafter abbreviated as TRC is a team formed by the agency in charge of Women's Empowerment and Children that is tasked with assisting UPT PPA in conducting outreach and/or assistance to accelerate the process of handling cases of violence against women and children.
25. Women's and Children's Protection Task Force is a coordinative institution formed by the Bulukumba Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Bulukumba Regency.
26. Vulnerable Groups are any person or community group entitled to receive more treatment and protection relating to their specificity. Vulnerable groups as referred to in this regulation consist of women and children in conflict with the law, persons with disabilities, Indonesian migrant workers, the elderly and/or indigenous peoples of ammatoa Kajang.

CHAPTER VIII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 25

1. The community may actively participate in providing protection for women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include: a. conducting prevention and reporting cases of violence against women and children that occur in their residential environment; b. providing emergency assistance if there is violence against women and children;

c. initiating the establishment of institutions for the protection of women and children at the regional, sub-district, village and sub-district levels;
d. participating in the protection of women and children through existing service institutions; and/or e. assisting in the process of repatriation, social rehabilitation, and social reintegration.

This house functions as a temporary, safe and confidential residence, where victims can receive psychological, legal, and social support for their recovery.

Paragraph (4) Sufficiently clear.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect and protection for the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status.

This means that women and children have equal rights to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

15 - Point b What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

Point c What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims as well as potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Point d What is meant by the principle of best interests for women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.

Point e What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. Every individual has equal rights to be protected from acts of violence, without exception Point f What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment of a group of people who experience physical and non-physical vulnerability or limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

Article 17

1. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 16, the Regent shall establish programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the form of a regional action plan as a basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing protection for women and children.
2. The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.

Article 7

1. Victim assistance as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2) letter f includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the victim's condition.
2. Victim assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by UPT PPA.
3. Victim assistance is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

SOUTH SULAWESI PROVINCE

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 28

1. Appointed officials, as referred to in Article 16 paragraph (4), if they fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, shall be subject to administrative actions and/or sanctions.
2. Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. verbal warning;
b. written warning; and c. other administrative sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Further provisions regarding the imposition of administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a regent regulation.

PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE

Article 5

3. Planning and implementation of policies, programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a namely:a. integrating women and children protection issues into the policies, programs and activities of Regional Apparatus; andb. making women and children protection issues one of the regional development priorities.
4. Provision of education as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b namely: a. providing information, guidance and/or counseling; b. providing accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement and social services;
c. creating a friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women; andd. building and providing an easily accessible information system; (5) Enhancement of Community participation through involvement of parties as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, namely:a. building and enhancing community participation and awareness towards prevention of women and children protection; b. making regional regulations and encouraging Village Governments to make Village Regulations related to protection of women and children; andc. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, private sector/business world, universities, mass media, and non-governmental organizations as well as community institutions that work and care for women and children.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect and protection for the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status.

This means that women and children have equal rights to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims as well as potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Point d What is meant by the principle of best interests for women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.

Point e What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. Every individual has equal rights to be protected from acts of violence, without exception Point f What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment of a group of people who experience physical and non-physical vulnerability or limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 25

d. participating in the protection of women and children through existing service institutions; and/or e. assisting in the process of repatriation, social rehabilitation, and social reintegration.

Article 7

1. Victim assistance as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2) letter f includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the victim's condition.
2. Victim assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by UPT PPA.

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 28

b. written warning; and c. other administrative sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

REGENT OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY

DECIDES:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

4. Regional Apparatus is an organization/Institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent in the context of administering government consisting of regional secretary, regional agencies and regional technical institutions, sub-districts, villages and civil service police units according to regional needs.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bulukumba Regency.
2. Government is a body or organization that exercises the governmental power of a state. The Government has the duty to administer governmental affairs, from the central, provincial, regency, municipal, sub-district, village, to hamlet levels.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an organization/Institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent in the context of administering government consisting of regional secretary, regional agencies and regional technical institutions, sub-districts, villages and civil service police units according to regional needs.
5. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the principal duties and functions in carrying out Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Bulukumba Regency.
6. Village Government is the administration of governmental affairs and the interests of the local community in the governmental system of the unitary state of the Republic of Indonesia.
7. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the annual financial plan of the regional government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and DPRD, and stipulated by Regional Regulation.
8. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBDes is the annual financial plan of the village government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Village Head and Village Representative Body which is stipulated through Village Regulation.

3 -

9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Implementation of Women's and Children's Protection is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Central Government, Regional Government, Village Government, and the community to fulfill the rights of women and children as citizens within the scope of this Regional Regulation.
11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women's and Children's Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
16. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, and deprivation of liberty arbitrarily whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
17. Victim is a person who experiences physical suffering, women and children who experience violence and/or mental threats and or economic loss resulting from an act of violence.
18. Victim of Violence is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from a criminal act of violence.
19. Violence Prevention is any action or effort undertaken to eliminate various factors that cause acts of violence against women and children.
20. Community is individual Indonesian citizens, community groups, and/or Mass Organizations.
21. Technical Implementation Unit for Women's and Children's Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an integrated service provider for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
22. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

4 -

23. Assistance for Victims of Violence is an effort or process to assist victims of violence in accessing the right to handling, protection, and recovery.
24. Rapid Reaction Team hereinafter abbreviated as TRC is a team formed by the agency in charge of Women's Empowerment and Children that is tasked with assisting UPT PPA in conducting outreach and/or assistance to accelerate the process of handling cases of violence against women and children.
25. Women's and Children's Protection Task Force is a coordinative institution formed by the Bulukumba Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Bulukumba Regency.
26. Vulnerable Groups are any person or community group entitled to receive more treatment and protection relating to their specificity. Vulnerable groups as referred to in this regulation consist of women and children in conflict with the law, persons with disabilities, Indonesian migrant workers, the elderly and/or indigenous peoples of ammatoa Kajang.

CHAPTER IV

PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE

Article 5

1. Prevention of violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a is implemented through:a. planning and implementation of policies, programs, and activities; b. provision of education; andc. enhancement of community participation.
2. Prevention of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented by the Regional Government in an integrated and sustainable manner based on the Regional Long-Term Development Plan and the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
3. Planning and implementation of policies, programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a namely:a. integrating women and children protection issues into the policies, programs and activities of Regional Apparatus; andb. making women and children protection issues one of the regional development priorities.
4. Provision of education as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b namely: a. providing information, guidance and/or counseling; b. providing accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement and social services;
c. creating a friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women; andd. building and providing an easily accessible information system; (5) Enhancement of Community participation through involvement of parties as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, namely:a. building and enhancing community participation and awareness towards prevention of women and children protection; b. making regional regulations and encouraging Village Governments to make Village Regulations related to protection of women and children; andc. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, private sector/business world, universities, mass media, and non-governmental organizations as well as community institutions that work and care for women and children.

CHAPTER VIII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 25

1. The community may actively participate in providing protection for women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include: a. conducting prevention and reporting cases of violence against women and children that occur in their residential environment; b. providing emergency assistance if there is violence against women and children;

12 -
c. initiating the establishment of institutions for the protection of women and children at the regional, sub-district, village and sub-district levels;
d. participating in the protection of women and children through existing service institutions; and/or e. assisting in the process of repatriation, social rehabilitation, and social reintegration.

Article 7

1. Victim assistance as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2) letter f includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the victim's condition.
2. Victim assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by UPT PPA.
3. Victim assistance is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect and protection for the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status.

This means that women and children have equal rights to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

15 - Point b What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

Point c What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims as well as potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Point d What is meant by the principle of best interests for women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.

Point e What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. Every individual has equal rights to be protected from acts of violence, without exception Point f What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment of a group of people who experience physical and non-physical vulnerability or limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

Article 17

1. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 16, the Regent shall establish programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the form of a regional action plan as a basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing protection for women and children.
2. The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

22. Article 2

Point a What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect and protection for the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status.

This means that women and children have equal rights to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

15 - Point b What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

Point c What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims as well as potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Point d What is meant by the principle of best interests for women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.

Point e What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. Every individual has equal rights to be protected from acts of violence, without exception Point f What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment of a group of people who experience physical and non-physical vulnerability or limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

Regional Apparatus is an organization/Institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent in the context of administering government consisting of regional secretary, regional agencies and regional technical institutions, sub-districts, villages and civil service police units according to regional needs.

9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Implementation of Women's and Children's Protection is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Central Government, Regional Government, Village Government, and the community to fulfill the rights of women and children as citizens within the scope of this Regional Regulation.
11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women's and Children's Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect and protection for the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status.

This means that women and children have equal rights to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

15 - Point b What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

Point c What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims as well as potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Point d What is meant by the principle of best interests for women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.

Point e What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. Every individual has equal rights to be protected from acts of violence, without exception Point f What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment of a group of people who experience physical and non-physical vulnerability or limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated the provision of protection for women and children, as well as granting equal rights to women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments that have the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment to providing protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled and to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region, so that efforts involving all parties in various aspects of development need to be carried out.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Government of Bulukumba Regency in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 26

Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and c. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bulukumba Regency.
2. Government is a body or organization that exercises the governmental power of a state. The Government has the duty to administer governmental affairs, from the central, provincial, regency, municipal, sub-district, village, to hamlet levels.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an organization/Institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent in the context of administering government consisting of regional secretary, regional agencies and regional technical institutions, sub-districts, villages and civil service police units according to regional needs.
5. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the principal duties and functions in carrying out Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Bulukumba Regency.
6. Village Government is the administration of governmental affairs and the interests of the local community in the governmental system of the unitary state of the Republic of Indonesia.
7. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the annual financial plan of the regional government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and DPRD, and stipulated by Regional Regulation.
8. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBDes is the annual financial plan of the village government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Village Head and Village Representative Body which is stipulated through Village Regulation.

9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Implementation of Women's and Children's Protection is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Central Government, Regional Government, Village Government, and the community to fulfill the rights of women and children as citizens within the scope of this Regional Regulation.
11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women's and Children's Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
16. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, and deprivation of liberty arbitrarily whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
17. Victim is a person who experiences physical suffering, women and children who experience violence and/or mental threats and or economic loss resulting from an act of violence.
18. Victim of Violence is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from a criminal act of violence.
19. Violence Prevention is any action or effort undertaken to eliminate various factors that cause acts of violence against women and children.
20. Community is individual Indonesian citizens, community groups, and/or Mass Organizations.
21. Technical Implementation Unit for Women's and Children's Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an integrated service provider for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
22. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

4 -

23. Assistance for Victims of Violence is an effort or process to assist victims of violence in accessing the right to handling, protection, and recovery.
24. Rapid Reaction Team hereinafter abbreviated as TRC is a team formed by the agency in charge of Women's Empowerment and Children that is tasked with assisting UPT PPA in conducting outreach and/or assistance to accelerate the process of handling cases of violence against women and children.
25. Women's and Children's Protection Task Force is a coordinative institution formed by the Bulukumba Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Bulukumba Regency.
26. Vulnerable Groups are any person or community group entitled to receive more treatment and protection relating to their specificity. Vulnerable groups as referred to in this regulation consist of women and children in conflict with the law, persons with disabilities, Indonesian migrant workers, the elderly and/or indigenous peoples of ammatoa Kajang.

CHAPTER IV

PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE

Article 5

1. Prevention of violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a is implemented through:a. planning and implementation of policies, programs, and activities; b. provision of education; andc. enhancement of community participation.
2. Prevention of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented by the Regional Government in an integrated and sustainable manner based on the Regional Long-Term Development Plan and the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
3. Planning and implementation of policies, programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a namely:a. integrating women and children protection issues into the policies, programs and activities of Regional Apparatus; andb. making women and children protection issues one of the regional development priorities.
4. Provision of education as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b namely: a. providing information, guidance and/or counseling; b. providing accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement and social services;
c. creating a friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women; andd. building and providing an easily accessible information system; (5) Enhancement of Community participation through involvement of parties as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, namely:a. building and enhancing community participation and awareness towards prevention of women and children protection; b. making regional regulations and encouraging Village Governments to make Village Regulations related to protection of women and children; andc. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, private sector/business world, universities, mass media, and non-governmental organizations as well as community institutions that work and care for women and children.

Part Four

Community Institutions and civil society organizations

Article 17

1. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 16, the Regent shall establish programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the form of a regional action plan as a basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing protection for women and children.
2. The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.

Article 7

1. Victim assistance as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2) letter f includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the victim's condition.
2. Victim assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by UPT PPA.
3. Victim assistance is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER X

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 28

1. Appointed officials, as referred to in Article 16 paragraph (4), if they fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, shall be subject to administrative actions and/or sanctions.
2. Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. verbal warning;
b. written warning; and c. other administrative sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Further provisions regarding the imposition of administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a regent regulation.
